text:
Maria G.: quick follow-up from the RFC — I ran a small perf sim for pushing RBAC checks into the tile read path (fastpath) vs keeping them in the authz sidecar. results look promising but there are tradeoffs.

Aj: can you summarize the perf gains and the operational cost?

Maria G.: perf: median latency for dashboard tile requests dropped ~70% in the sim (580ms -> ~170ms) and p95 improved similarly. reason: eliminating an extra RPC and enabling prefix cache hits without authz post-filtering.

Kevin: nice. how do we handle cache invalidation? coupling auth rules to tile cache sounds risky.

Maria G.: that's the main downside. two risks: (1) cache staleness when a user's permissions change, (2) complexity of embedding tenant-aware rules in low-level storage.

Sophia: for regulated tenants we can't risk stale permissions. that suggests a hybrid approach.

Dave: quick proposal: hybrid handoff model — pushdown authz for anonymous/low-sensitivity dashboards where speed matters, and sidecar-checks for high-sensitivity/enterprise tenants. we can use tenant flags to choose path.

Aj: hybrid seems pragmatic. what about code surface area? we've already got tiling logic in C++ runtime, authz currently in Go sidecar. pushing logic into runtime increases coupling and testing burden.

Maria G.: agreed. implementation sketch I shared in the RFC thread: add a tiny auth predicate evaluator in the runtime (only supports allow/deny lookups + user-id, role checks). full policy language stays in authz service. runtime caches small allow lists per tile with TTL.

Kevin: show pseudo.

Maria G.: ```
// in runtime tile read path
if (tenantConfig.fastpathAuthz == PUSHDOWN) {
  if (!runtimeAuthCheck(tileId, userId)) return 403;
  return cachedTile;
} else {
  // call sidecar as today
  return callAuthzSidecarThenRead();
}
```

Sophia: TTL strategy? short TTL (30s) handles most cases but doesn't satisfy immediate revocation. we need explicit revocation hooks from admin actions.

Dave: we can wire admin-change events into a cache invalidation stream. that avoids long TTLs. but we must guarantee ordering + delivery for enterprise SLAs.

Aj: delivery guarantees will be expensive. ops impact?

ops-bot: deploy window suggestion: canary 24h on low-traffic region, feature flag gated per-tenant.

Maria G.: proposed rollout plan: 1) implement runtime predicate evaluator (simple, feature-flagged) 2) expose tenant opt-in config (fastpath: pushdown | sidecar | hybrid) 3) implement invalidation stream + admin hooks 4) canary low-traffic region 24–72h 5) monitor auth-fail spikes and cache coherence metrics.

Kevin: metrics to add: auth-fail rate, cache-hit by tenant, revocation latency, p95 for fastpath requests. set alert thresholds.

Sophia: need compliance checklist for enterprise tenants before enabling pushdown: audit logging for every auth decision (even if cached), revocation SLA, and KMS integration for any key material used by runtime.

Maria G.: noted — runtime will emit structured audit events to the control plane; will not store secrets.

Dave: open questions: how many predicates can we support in runtime without bloat? right now we plan allowlist + role membership lookups; any other immediate needs?

Aj: maybe add tenant-scoped feature-flag checks (for product gating) but avoid full ABAC. keep runtime minimal.

Kevin: timeline?

Maria G.: rough: proto impl (2 wks) -> internal perf tests (1 wk) -> invalidation hook (1 wk) -> canary rollout (1–2 wks) -> iterate. total ~6–8 weeks with a small team.

Sophia: thumbs-up for staged rollout + hard opt-out for enterprise until compliance signoff.

Dave: I'll sketch the invalidation stream design and owner it.

Maria G.: action items: 
- Dave: design invalidation stream + failure modes (due EOD Wed)
- Kevin: metrics + alerts spec (EOD Thu)
- Aj: test harness for runtime auth predicate (POC by next Tue)
- Sophia: compliance checklist draft (EOD Fri)

Aj: sounds good. tagging eng-sre for alerting help.

Maria G.: thanks all. can we reconvene after the EOD artifacts? :eyes:

Kevin: :shipit:
